result.title: InertiaMPDD: Multimodal Personalized Depression Detection via Emotional Inertia-Inspired Dynamics Modeling
result.summary: Multimodal depression screening estimates risk from speech, visual behavior and language. Current methods mainly predict labels, with limited evidence of departures from a non-depressed reference. Recording-level supervision also leaves fine-grained emotional dynamics unannotated. Motivated by emotional inertia, the persistence of affect, InertiaMPDD learns healthy next-state patterns using a world-model-inspired latent predictor. Using pretrained multimodal representations, it predicts from observed history and context. Reference deviation, residual decay rate and a Jacobian spectral descriptor form reference-derived emotional dynamics descriptors, evaluated as candidate proxy biomarkers for standalone screening and personalized decision correction. Across five cohorts from four datasets, fusion reaches 98.41% F1 on D-Vlog and 84.98% on LMVD. Standalone descriptors outperform fixed additive fusion on MPDD but discriminate weakly on AVEC2014. These findings distinguish reference informativeness from fusion benefit and reveal context-dependent utility.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 InertiaMPDD：受「情绪惯性」启发，用预训练多模态表示构建类世界模型的 latent 预测器学习健康下一状态模式，并将参考偏差、残差衰减率与 Jacobian 谱描述子作为抑郁筛查与个体化决策校正的候选代理指标。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 latent 下一状态预测、残差衰减率与 Jacobian 谱描述子，可能可供核查如何刻画 LVR 中隐推理状态随步骤或深度的漂移与收敛；但研究问题属抑郁筛查应用，而非 VLM 推理本身。
